title: Warm springs moved frog calling seasons 2-3 days earlier per 1 C on northeastern and midwestern US NAAMP routes in 2001-2015 and biased naive detection indices down for early and up for late species
abstract: Question: do anuran calling seasons move earlier in warm springs, do volunteer survey dates follow, and does the remaining mismatch bias naive detection indices? Data: 19,299 North American Amphibian Monitoring Program (NAAMP) survey runs on 1,177 routes in 25 eastern and central US states, 2001-2015 (USGS, public domain), and monthly GHCN-CAMS temperature anomalies. Method: for 38 species-region units, a logit model with route x observer effects moved a seasonal detection curve by delta days per 1 C of spring anomaly, with survey-night air temperature and wind as controls; year-block bootstrap intervals. The plan was written before the outcome models. Results: all 18 Northeast (NE) and Midwest (MW) units had delta below zero (inverse-variance means -2.4 and -3.0 days per C; 15 of 16 stable units negative in both 2001-2008 and 2009-2015; robust to observer control, temperature window, level term and removal of 2012). In the Southeast (SE), the mean was -1.1 and only 1 of 20 intervals was below zero. Volunteers moved the first survey window by -2.5 (NE), -1.9 (MW) and -0.7 (SE) days per C and the last window not at all. Naive detection rates fell after warm springs for early species (wood frog -3.6% per C NE, -2.5% MW, -11.1% SE) and rose for late species (green frog +3.7% NE, +5.7% MW). A season-minus-survey mismatch model predicted these responses across 34 units (r = 0.59). Without the volunteer date shift, the wood frog bias would be about 2.6 times larger. Out of sample, models fitted without 2012 predicted the record-warm 2012 spring better with the shift than without it in 10 of 11 MW and 5 of 7 NE units, but not in the SE; the linear shift explained only part of the 2012 decrease in early-species detections. With about 0.3 C per decade spring warming at NE routes, the bias is about -0.7% per decade for wood frog and +1.1% for green frog: small, but of opposite sign for early and late species. Limitations: monthly gridded temperature, a fixed curve shape, binary run detection, no data after 2015, broad SE region, correlational design.
